title: A Reader can advance to a numbered record

notes.author: Jack Roddy/d58bf845
notes.text: `count` as a free fn reads as 'count this source'. As a constructor-and-method it invites counting and then reusing a consumed reader. Leaning free fn.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/d58bf845
notes.text: Both names are nearly taken: `index::count_in(path)` reads a count out of an index file's header, and `Index::position(name)` looks a record up by name. A free `index::count` beside `count_in`, and `Reader::position` beside `Index::position`, differ in what they answer and not in what they are called.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/d58bf845
notes.text: `advance_to` asked to go backwards panics: the caller broke the contract, the same argument as `Indexable::get`'s invariant.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/c45d6630
notes.text: Left the milestone sail-31fdd9. This is streaming over one file and has no multi-file content. Ready to build on its own.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text:
Built on `dev`, not yet committed. `index::count`, `Reader::position`, `Reader::advance_to`, and the same two methods on `lines::Rows` are in, with tests in `reader_tests` and `lines::tests`. `sail skim`'s streaming arm uses `advance_to`, and `sail skim` and `sail count` use `count`.

`sail get`'s streaming loop was left as it is. Its error for a position past the end reports how many records the input holds, and `advance_to` returning `false` leaves `position()` at `None`, so the loop would need its own counter back.

`offset()` after `advance` returns `false` still reports a stale start with zero length. sail-427b32 covers that state.
